findings.title: Shipped YAML catalogs lack 1h write price
findings.problem: missing-adoption-gap: CatalogPricer.price prices 1h cache-write tokens at CostConfig.cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_1hr, but none of the Claude models in config/llms/llm-dial-config.yaml or config/llms/llm-aws-config.yaml define it (10 cache_creation_input_token_cost entries, 0 _above_1hr). LLM_PROXY_ENABLED defaults to False, so catalog_source() is 'yaml' unless the proxy is on. No test loads the shipped YAML; every money test patches get_all_llm_model_info with a catalog that has the 1h price. The MR documents this as a deliberate deviation (1h tokens at 0 plus unpriced_models).
findings.impact: In proxy-off deployments every Claude Code cache write carrying a 1h split prices at $0 (previously the producer cost counted it, and unsplit writes priced at 5m), so COST, per user/model/session/repository money, bloat_pct and Wasted are understated - the opposite of the ticket's complaint that 1h writes were under-priced. Consumer: LLMService.get_all_llm_model_info reading the YAML when catalog_source() == 'yaml'.
findings.recommendation: Get a human decision: either add cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_1hr to every Claude model in config/llms/llm-dial-config.yaml and config/llms/llm-aws-config.yaml that has cache_creation_input_token_cost (and add a config test loading the shipped YAML and asserting a positive 1h price via CatalogPricer under catalog_source 'yaml'), or explicitly accept the documented deviation (1h writes at $0 plus unpriced_models) for proxy-off deployments.
